individuals.treatment_summary: Self-administered colchicine and low-dose prednisolone (0-5 mg/day, self-increased to 6-10 mg/day); PSL 3.5 mg/day on admission; PSL 20 mg for acute sensorineural hearing loss, tapered to 5 mg; increased PSL plus methotrexate 12 mg/week with poor response; then adalimumab, after which oral ulcers disappeared, inflammatory signs became negative and no further diplopia; colchicine discontinued owing to diarrhea; prednisolone tapered to 2 mg/day. Table 2 current treatment: GC, MTX, & ADA
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Previously diagnosed with incomplete Behçet disease at 28 years of age; neuro-Behçet disease suspected but not confirmed. Gene panel testing for hereditary autoinflammatory diseases (K010-14_v13, Kazusa DNA Research Institute) revealed heterozygous TNFAIP3 c.259C>T (R87X), previously reported in two families with HA20; NF-kB luciferase reporter assay showed impaired inhibition; 'On the basis of these findings, the patient was diagnosed with HA20.' HLA-B51 negative; no RELA variants.

variants.parental_testing_statement: Genetic testing has not been conducted on any of his relatives at present.
variants.functional_evidence_statement: NF-kB luciferase reporter assay in A20-deficient HEK293 cells with TNF-alpha stimulation: R87X showed considerably higher luciferase activity than wild-type, indicating impaired inhibition of NF-kB activity

variants.pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors: assessed to have limited disease relevance
